title: SBA 504 Loan Origination Software: Features, iCAP, and How to Choose
summary: SBA 504 origination software runs CDC–lender deals in one workflow. Choose API-first tools built for the 504 structure and SBA's iCAP shift.
body_markdown:
### What is SBA 504 loan origination software?


SBA 504 loan origination software runs intake, eligibility, documentation, underwriting, and CDC–lender coordination for 504 projects in one shared workflow. It gives the borrower, the third-party lender, and the Certified Development Company (CDC) one record of every file. That record follows the deal from first application to closing.


A 504 loan needs more than a generic or 7(a) tool. Each deal pairs a CDC debenture loan on a second lien with a third-party lender loan on a first lien, plus a borrower contribution. That makes 504 origination a multi-party data problem, not a form-filling problem.


The volume is real. The U.S. Small Business Administration reported approximately 6,750 504 loans for $7.8 billion in its[SBA FY2025 lending results](https://www.sba.gov/article/2025/09/30/trump-sba-delivers-record-capital-small-businesses-fy25) . Those figures are preliminary, since SBA released them before the fiscal year closed.


‍


### How the 504 structure shapes origination workflows


Every SBA 504 lender works inside a tri-party capital stack. The software has to model that stack natively—or teams end up rebuilding it in spreadsheets for every deal.


The sections below translate the core rules of the SBA 504 loan program into system requirements. These are implications for software design drawn from the regulations, not requirements SBA places on vendors.


#### The 50/40/10 split and borrower contribution


Under the eCFR / Code of Federal Regulations[504 financing structure rules](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/section-120.801) , a CDC debenture funds up to 40% on a second lien. The borrower contributes at least 10%. A third-party lender covers the remaining balance of project costs on a first lien.


The eCFR / Code of Federal Regulations[504 borrower contribution rule](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/section-120.910) raises the borrower's 10% floor in two cases. It's 15% for a new business or a limited or single-purpose building, and 20% if both apply.


The lender share has a floor too. Under the Code of Federal Regulations[13 CFR 120.920 lender participation](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/section-120.920) rule, third-party loans must total at least as much as the 504 loan. That minimum rises to 50% of project cost for a business operating two years or less or a limited or single-purpose asset.


Origination software should calculate the required injection and lender minimum automatically from business age and property type. Skip manual math—let the system set the contribution tier at intake and recalculate when project costs change.


#### Eligibility and size checks


A business can qualify under its industry size standard or an alternative test. The eCFR / Code of Federal Regulations[SBA alternative size standard](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/section-121.301) caps tangible net worth at $20 million. Average net income can't exceed $6.5 million, affiliates included.


Software should pull financials, flag affiliates, and check those thresholds before a file reaches the CDC. Replace manual threshold checks with real-time data and live credit signals through[credit underwriting and decisioning](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/credit-underwriting-and-decisioning) that adapts as data flows in.


#### Eligible uses and owner occupancy


An SBA 504 real estate loan is built for buildings, land, and long-term machinery and equipment. The U.S. Small Business Administration's[SBA 504 eligible uses](https://www.sba.gov/loans/504-loans/) page states that a 504 loan cannot be used for working capital or inventory. Eligible equipment must have a useful remaining life of at least 10 years.


Occupancy rules add another check. The eCFR / Code of Federal Regulations[SBA owner-occupancy requirements](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-13/section-120.131) set a minimum of 51% occupancy for existing property and 60% for new construction. Software should flag ineligible uses and occupancy gaps at intake, before anyone orders an appraisal.

#### Document management and application completeness


A 504 loan file is document-heavy. SBA's Form 1244 (05-2020 edition), issued by the U.S. Small Business Administration, lists the[SBA Form 1244 exhibits](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/DownloadDocument?objectID=101534001) for each application.


Each owner of 20% or more provides a personal financial statement (Form 413) current within 90 days and last year's federal tax returns. The business adds a balance sheet and income statement dated within 120 days.


That edition also lists an independent appraisal for project real estate, plus contractor estimates and vendor quotes for machinery and equipment. It calls for a letter of intent from the third-party lender, and it has the CDC upload the completed application to E-Tran. Confirm the current form edition and SBA's SOP 50 10 with the CDC, since requirements can change between editions.


Software should set dynamic document requirements based on the project, then analyze uploads automatically. Use an[SBA loan document checklist](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-loan-document-checklist-every-document-you-need-stage-by-stage) to map requirements by stage.


Skip manual file review—use[AI document analysis with Doc Analyzer](https://www.lendflow.com/solutions/doc-analyzer) to extract data and flag gaps. Complete files reach underwriting faster and need less back-and-forth with the borrower.


#### Compliance, fraud screening, and CDC–lender coordination


Fraud and KYB screening belongs at the start of the workflow. Early screening protects both the lender and the CDC from spending time on risky files. For a practical framework, see our guide to[building a fraud detection stack](https://www.lendflow.com/post/fraud-detection-stack) .


Owner and affiliate information should be collected and verified in one place. Shared status tracking and a full audit history give every SBA 504 lender and CDC partner the same view of the deal.

### What SBA's iCAP means for 504 origination


The U.S. Small Business Administration announced iCAP on Nov 5, 2026, as the platform that will replace ETRAN and the Capital Access Financial System (CAFS). As of Nov 2026, iCAP origination covers 7(a) lending only. Per[SBA's iCAP announcement](https://www.sba.gov/article/2026/11/05/sba-launches-icap-modernize-7a-loan-origination-streamline-workflows-accelerate-small-business) , the U.S. Small Business Administration's roadmap includes adding 504 origination, servicing, and liquidation.


SBA has not published a date for 504 in iCAP, and the current milestones apply to 7(a) only. The 7(a) origination API is scheduled for production in December 2026, and 7(a) lenders must migrate from the ETRAN origination interface by June 2027. The launch followed a six-month pilot, and SBA reports that more than 250 lenders have joined iCAP to date, processing 2,000 loans.


For the SBA 504 loan program, the takeaway is to prepare without guessing. CDCs and 504 lenders should keep current ETRAN integrations stable, using resources like our[SBA E-Tran API integration](https://www.lendflow.com/post/sba-e-tran-api-integration-practical-guide-for-lenders-and-fintech-teams) guide. They should also choose API-first software with open architecture that can swap SBA endpoints without rebuilding workflows.


‍


### How to choose SBA 504 loan origination software


Most 7(a) tools aren't plug-and-play for 504. They assume one lender, one loan, and one lien, while every SBA 504 deal adds a CDC, a second loan, and tiered contribution rules.


Use this checklist when evaluating any 504 lender platform:


- **Native 504 structure modeling:** Tracks the lender loan, CDC debenture, and borrower injection together.
- **Configurable eligibility rules:** Updates size, use, occupancy, and contribution rules without code changes.
- **SBA system integration and iCAP readiness:** Supports current ETRAN connections and adapts as SBA endpoints change.
- **CDC–lender collaboration:** Shares status, documents, and messages across both parties.
- **Document automation:** Sets dynamic requirements and analyzes uploads automatically.
- **Reporting:** Shows pipeline, conversion, and time-to-close across every deal.
- **Implementation speed:** Launches with widgets, landing pages, and APIs instead of long build cycles.
- **Vendor roadmap:** Shows a clear plan for SBA modernization and new data sources.

### FAQs


#### How does an SBA 504 loan work?


A CDC funds up to 40% of project costs on a second lien, and a third-party lender covers the remaining balance on a first lien. The borrower contributes 10% to 20%, depending on business age and property type.


#### Is 504 origination available in iCAP?


Not yet—as of Nov 2026, iCAP origination covers 7(a) lending only. 504 origination is on SBA's roadmap, with no date published.


#### What documents does a 504 application require?


SBA's Form 1244 (05-2020 edition) lists a personal financial statement and last year's tax returns for each 20%+ owner, plus recent business financials. It also lists a real estate appraisal, contractor estimates or vendor quotes, and a third-party lender letter of intent.


#### Can a 504 loan fund working capital?


No—SBA states that a 504 loan cannot be used for working capital or inventory. It funds buildings, land, and long-term machinery and equipment instead.


#### Why can't lenders use 7(a) software for 504 loans?


A 504 deal involves two loans, two liens, a CDC as a third party, and tiered borrower contribution rules. Most 7(a) software isn't built to model that structure.
